title: Adjunctions of the datum
statement:
Use the finite-field, coefficient, scheme and operation conventions of [def-fix-six-functor-datum], with $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ and a separated finite-type morphism $f:X\to Y$ between finite-type $k$-schemes. Integral pullback means completed pullback; rationalization is raw scalar localization and algebraically closed coefficients use common finite stages. Then:

1. The derived operations restrict to an adjunction $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ between $D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ and $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$. Its unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to Rf_*Lf^*$ and counit $\varepsilon_f:Lf^*Rf_*\to\mathrm{id}$ satisfy
$$ (Rf_*\varepsilon_f)\circ(\eta_fRf_*)=\mathrm{id}_{Rf_*},\qquad (\varepsilon_fLf^*)\circ(Lf^*\eta_f)=\mathrm{id}_{Lf^*}.$$
2. If $f$ is exceptionally admissible in the sense of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility], the constructible exceptional functor of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] is right adjoint to $Rf_!$ on $D^b_c$, with unit $\nu_f:\mathrm{id}\to Rf^!Rf_!$ and counit $\mu_f:Rf_!Rf^!\to\mathrm{id}$. These satisfy both triangle identities and agree under compactification-refinement comparisons. The same Hom bijections restrict to $Rf_!:D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)\rightleftarrows D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda):Rf^!$. This conditional assertion does not assert existence of an unrestricted ambient pro-etale exceptional adjoint.
3. For composable separated finite-type morphisms $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$, write ordinary composition comparisons in the adjunction-compatible normalization: the direct-image comparison is conjugate to the pullback-composition comparison [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Under these comparisons the composite ordinary unit and counit are
$$\eta_{gf}=(Rg_*\eta_f Lg^*)\circ\eta_g,\qquad \varepsilon_{gf}=\varepsilon_f\circ(Lf^*\varepsilon_g Rf_*).$$
When $f,g,gf$ satisfy the exceptional hypothesis of (2), the compact-support composition isomorphism of [thm-sf-comp-composition], and its completed and transported forms on the corresponding domains of [fix-lem-exchanges], has conjugate isomorphism
$$R(gf)^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^!Rg^!.$$
The composite exceptional unit and counit, transported along this isomorphism, are
$$\nu_{gf}=(Rf^!\nu_g Rf_!)\circ\nu_f,\qquad \mu_{gf}=\mu_g\circ(Rg_!\mu_f Rg^!).$$
The assertion is formal in the specified adjunctions and composition comparisons; no composition theorem on arbitrary ambient pro-etale inputs is implicit.
4. For a Cartesian square $X'\xrightarrow{g'}X$, $Y'\xrightarrow gY$, with vertical maps $f',f$, use the transformations of [def-exchange-projection], retaining exactly the coefficient and domain conventions of [fix-lem-exchanges]. Suppose the exceptional adjunctions needed below are available as in (2). The direct-image exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_*:Lg^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*Lg'^*$ is the mate of the pullback square: its transpose is
$$Lf'^*Lg^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{\theta Rf_*}Lg'^*Lf^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{Lg'^*\varepsilon_f}Lg'^*.$$
The exceptional-inverse-image exchange associated to $\operatorname{Ex}_!:Lg^*Rf_!\to Rf'_!Lg'^*$ is its conjugate under the composite adjunctions
$$Lg^*Rf_!\dashv Rf^!Rg_*,\qquad Rf'_!Lg'^*\dashv Rg'_*Rf'^!.$$
Thus its type is $Rg'_*Rf'^!\to Rf^!Rg_*$. Wherever $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ is an isomorphism on these domains, its conjugate is the corresponding identification $Rg'_*Rf'^!\cong Rf^!Rg_*$. These transposes respect refinement comparisons and pasting on the same domains. No general implication that an arbitrary square mate of an isomorphism is invertible is asserted.

proof.text: At $A=A_{E,n}$, [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] supplies the actual natural derived Hom bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_X(Lf^*M,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(M,Rf_*K)$ on the ordinary unbounded pro-etale categories. Its left functor preserves bounded constructibility by [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-preserves-bounded-constructible]. For its right functor write $K\cong\nu_X^*H$ using [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. The morphism $f$ is qcqs (it is separated and finite type), so [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] identifies $Rf_*K$ with $\nu_Y^*Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}H$. By [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] the latter is bounded constructible. Both full subcategories therefore contain the values of both functors. Their Hom sets are the ambient Hom sets, so the same bijection gives the restricted adjunction. To check the coefficient convention of the pullback lemma, take the adic ring to be $\mathcal O_E$ with ideal $(\varpi_E)$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] this ring is a Noetherian domain with finite residue field; its quotients are finite by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Each quotient is perfect over $\mathcal O_E$, represented by the finite-free resolution $[\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{\varpi_E^n}\mathcal O_E]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$. Thus its $P_n$ is exactly $A_{E,n}$; its additive exponent is a power of $\ell$ and is invertible over $k$.

For integral coefficients apply [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction] with $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi_E)$. Transport its Hom bijection through [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. The left functor is the completed pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]: the equivalence identifies its finite quotient tower and completion unit. For the right functor use [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison]. It supplies the completed/constant restriction comparison, its compatibility as a strict coefficient-diagram comparison, and the projection-normalized isomorphism $Rf_{*,R}K\cong R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRf_{*,n}K_n$. Thus the transported right adjoint is exactly the integral functor of [def-weil-derived-direct-image], rather than an independently chosen functor with isomorphic finite values. Completed pullback preserves $D^b_c$ by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible], and this direct image preserves it by [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible]. Restrict the bijection to the full subcategories. The Noetherian and finitely generated ideal hypotheses hold by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]: $\mathcal O_E$ is a principal ideal domain and $(\varpi_E)$ is principal.

At $E$, tensor the integral $\mathcal O_E$-linear Hom bijection and its inverse with $E$. By the Hom formula of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] the results are inverse bijections of the desired rational Hom sets; the functors and transformations are their scalar extensions by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]. The required linearity and finite-field-extension compatibility of these actual bijections are [lem-pur-ordinary-adjunction-scalar-compatibility], for precisely the comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, represent both objects and a morphism over a common finite field as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and take its adjunct there. If two representatives agree at a further field, the helper's scalar-compatibility equations make their adjuncts agree there; the same holds for inverse adjuncts. This defines inverse maps on colimit Hom sets, since their composites are identities at each finite stage. Naturality is likewise the finite-stage naturality. The scalar-comparison scheme hypotheses hold by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], since the schemes are finite type over $k$.

For each natural Hom bijection $h:\operatorname{Hom}(LM,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,RN)$ constructed above, set $\eta_M=h(1_{LM})$ and $\varepsilon_N=h^{-1}(1_{RN})$. Naturality gives $h(a)=R(a)\eta_M$ and $h^{-1}(b)=\varepsilon_N L(b)$. Applying $h^{-1}h$ to $1_{LM}$ gives $\varepsilon_{LM}L(\eta_M)=1_{LM}$; applying $hh^{-1}$ to $1_{RN}$ gives $R(\varepsilon_N)\eta_{RN}=1_{RN}$. These are both displayed ordinary triangle identities and will also give the exceptional ones.

source.place: Proof, Steps 1 and 2; Stacks Tag 0037, categories-definition-adjoint and the following discussion

proof.text: For the exceptional pair use the natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!K,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,Rf^!L)$ explicitly stated in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], for bounded constructible $K,L$ at each of the four coefficient stages. Thus the unit and counit are the images of the identity maps under these bijections and their inverses; the preceding calculation proves both triangles. This uses the constructible exceptional functor, not an unrestricted ambient right adjoint. Under the optional hypothesis of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility], the finite ambient adjoint and its constructible restriction identify with this functor by the representing Hom bijections stated in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Refinement comparisons identify the chosen adjunction maps by clause (1) of admissibility. At the higher stages keep its specified finite-system compatibility data; the constructible adjunction is the one already characterized above, so no existence of a new ambient adjoint is inferred.

Check the left functor before restricting to finite Tor amplitude. At finite coefficients choose $f=pj$ as in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Extension by zero is exact with the stalk description of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Extend the finite stratification of each constructible cohomology sheaf by the complementary closed stratum with zero sheaf. This proves that $j_!$ preserves bounded constructibility. Applying the finite direct-image argument of the first step to $p$ shows that $Rp_*j_!$ is bounded constructible. Under the comparison of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] this is also the ordinary etale compact-support functor on the etale origin. The same conclusion holds for $A_{E,1}$ and for every bounded constructible input.

source.place: Proof, Step 2: restriction to finite-Tor subcategories

proof.text:
Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and put $\kappa=A_{E,1}$. By clause (i) of [lem-sf-tensor-ctf], $K\otimes_A^L\kappa$ is bounded constructible: its first factor is finite Tor and its second is the bounded constructible constant residue sheaf; no finite-Tor hypothesis on the latter over $A$ is needed. The preceding step makes both $F=Rf_!K$ and $G=Rf_{!,\kappa}(K\otimes_A^L\kappa)$ bounded constructible. By [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] there is an isomorphism $F\otimes_A^L\kappa\cong G$. Choose integers $a\leq b$ outside which $G$ has zero cohomology; take $[0,0]$ if $G=0$. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] as used in step 1, write $F\cong
u_Y^*H$ with $H$ bounded constructible on the etale site. The tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identifies $F\otimes_A^L\kappa$ with $
u_Y^*(H\otimes_A^L\kappa)$, using the constant residue sheaf on each site. Exactness of $
u_Y^*$ gives $
u_Y^*\mathcal H^i(H\otimes_A^L\kappa)=0$ for $i
otin[a,b]$. These degree-zero sheaves vanish: the fully faithful comparison of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] reflects their zero identity maps. Therefore [lem-exc-residue-tor-test], applied to $H$, gives its Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Now [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval] gives the same interval for $F$ on the full pro-etale site. This proves preservation by the left functor before restricting the exceptional adjunction.

The right functor preserves finite Tor amplitude at the finite stage by clause (3) of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] and its identification in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Integrally the compact-support functor preserves bounded constructibility by [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible], and the exceptional functor does so by [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor], every object of either integral bounded constructible category already has uniform finite Tor amplitude. At field coefficients $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Hence in each case both functors preserve the indicated full subcategories. For objects in them the same Hom bijection is still a bijection between their Hom sets; its identity transposes are the same unit and counit. This proves the restricted exceptional adjunction without inferring left-functor preservation from right-functor preservation.

source.place: Proof, Step 2: restriction at every coefficient stage

proof.text: Paste the ordinary Hom bijections in the order $\operatorname{Hom}_X(Lf^*Lg^*M,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Lg^*M,Rf_*K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(M,Rg_*Rf_*K)$. The composite-adjunction formulas in [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], clause (2), with $L_1=Lg^*$ and $L_3=Lf^*$, give the unit $(Rg_*\eta_f Lg^*)\eta_g$ and counit $\varepsilon_f(Lf^*\varepsilon_g Rf_*)$. The pullback comparison has finite-stage type $L(gf)^*\cong Lf^*Lg^*$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Use the conjugate comparison of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] on the right, as specified in the statement; conjugation transports the two Hom bijections and therefore both units and counits. At integral and field stages use the same adjunction-compatible normalization of the corresponding completed and transported pullback comparisons. This is a formula for the adjunction under that normalization, not a claim that arbitrary unrelated choices of composition comparisons preserve units. For the higher-stage existence of the ordinary composition comparisons, use [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition]: its integral hypothesis $Rf_*K\in D^b_c$ and its field-stage hypotheses on the further outputs hold by steps 2 and 3. Inverting the conjugation bijection gives the corresponding left composition isomorphism. Choose the comparisons in precisely this adjunction-compatible normalization, so there is no uncited theorem identifying independently chosen units.

Paste the exceptional Hom bijections to get $Rg_!Rf_!\dashv Rf^!Rg^!$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], now with $L_1=Rf_!$ and $L_3=Rg_!$, gives exactly $(Rf^!\nu_g Rf_!)\nu_f$ and $\mu_g(Rg_!\mu_f Rg^!)$. Let $\alpha:Rg_!Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(gf)_!$ be [thm-sf-comp-composition] at the finite stage, restricted to bounded constructible etale-origin inputs. At the other stages retain the completed and transported composition identifications asserted on their corresponding domains in [fix-lem-exchanges], clauses (2) and (4). Conjugation [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] applied to $\alpha$ gives $R(gf)^!\to Rf^!Rg^!$; applying it to $\alpha^{-1}$ gives its inverse, because conjugation reverses composition and sends identities to identities. The two composite Hom bijections agree through these conjugate isomorphisms, so their transposes of identities agree: their units and counits are the pasted ones. All exceptional pairs used here satisfy the hypothesis of clause (2).

For the square in clause (4), [def-exchange-projection] defines $\operatorname{Ex}_{*,K}=Rf'_*(Lg'^*\varepsilon_{f,K}\circ\theta_{Rf_*K})\circ\eta_{f',Lg^*Rf_*K}$. Under $Lf'^*\dashv Rf'_*$ the inverse Hom bijection sends this map to $Lg'^*\varepsilon_{f,K}\circ\theta_{Rf_*K}$: this is exactly the inverse-transpose identity proved from the triangles above. It is also the specialized formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. This proves the claimed direct-image transpose, with all compositions typed as displayed and with the supplied higher-stage comparison data required by the definition.

Set $A=Lg^*Rf_!$, $B=Rf'_!Lg'^*$, $R_A=Rf^!Rg_*$ and $R_B=Rg'_*Rf'^!$. The composite adjunction formulas of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] give $A\dashv R_A$, $B\dashv R_B$. Put $e=\operatorname{Ex}_!:A\to B$ as defined in [def-exchange-projection]. Apply [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] with $L_2=A$, $L_1=B$. Its formula is the typed composite $R_B\xrightarrow{\eta_A R_B}R_AAR_B\xrightarrow{R_A e R_B}R_ABR_B\xrightarrow{R_A\varepsilon_B}R_A$, precisely the stated exceptional comparison. If $e$ is invertible, the conjugate of $e^{-1}$ is inverse to this map, by the identity and composition laws of conjugation. This is conjugation between two entire left adjoints; it does not assert invertibility for arbitrary square mates. The domain qualifications in the statement ensure that all four constituent adjunctions and both composites are present.

Refinement and pasting compatibilities are equalities of these same composites. For refinements the component exceptional units and counits agree by [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility], and the exchange maps agree on the specified domains by [fix-lem-exchanges], clause (4). Applying the conjugate bijection to the equality gives equality of the exceptional comparisons; applying the inverse transpose gives equality of the direct-image transposes. For pasting, substitute the composite units and counits computed above into the mate formulas. Clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identify the result with the composite of the component mates, and clause (3) handles a change by a refinement comparison. Together with the horizontal and vertical exchange identities of [fix-lem-exchanges], clause (2), these give exactly the claimed compatibilities, on the same coefficient domains and with the same composition comparisons.
